rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should explore a promising multimodal configuration. config_002 uses scgpt (RNA) and resnet50 (image) with weighted fusion, which are strong encoders for multimodal tasks. Testing this configuration clarifies the effectiveness of combining these encoders with weighted fusion, balancing exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt and resnet50 have moderate performance. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer, which could capture more complex interactions. It clarifies whether aggregation method significantly impacts accuracy, balancing exploitation of the current setup with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and weighted fusion (like config_002) achieve higher accuracy than transformer aggregation (config_012). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 while keeping avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, which are key components of the current best. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice is the main driver of performance, addressing uncertainty about encoder impact while staying close to the promising multimodal multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows config_009 (rna_only) achieves the highest accuracy (0.677). This experiment tests rna_only with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation, which could clarify if different aggregation methods improve performance. It balances exploration of key design choices (aggregation) while staying within the rna_only modality that has shown strong results.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder (config_009) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_009) with transformer aggregation, which could improve performance by better capturing interactions between modalities. This clarifies whether aggregation method is a key factor in achieving high accuracy, balancing exploitation of the scvi_n200-resnet50 combination with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

Existing evidence shows config_010 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced image encoder) while keeping the proven RNA encoder and aggregation/fusion setup. This balances exploitation (building on successful components) and exploration (testing a stronger image encoder). The choice prioritizes reducing uncertainty about image encoder impact, which is critical for improving accuracy further.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_026) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder with the same high-performing setup could further improve accuracy, clarifying if RNA encoder choice is critical. It is the best use of the remaining budget to exploit the promising direction of transformer aggregation and weighted fusion.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_026) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method to avgpool (config_047) could yield better results, clarifying the importance of aggregation strategy. It directly explores a key design choice with high potential to improve performance.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_026) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which could clarify if alternative aggregation/fusion methods improve performance. It balances exploitation of proven components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) with exploration of different fusion strategies, maximizing the chance to find the optimal configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_026: 0.7249). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with concat fusion (vs. weighted fusion in config_026) to determine if combining these components differently could improve accuracy further. It directly addresses uncertainty about fusion method effectiveness under the top-performing RNA/image encoder pair.
